evidence_items.locator: Paragraph immediately before High on vibes, low on reasoning
evidence_items.explanation: The article offers a strongly critical assessment while also reporting Karpathy's favorable reaction. This supports the mixed-reception component; Marcus's own comments in the article are not used.

Pre-release autonomy and research-engineering tests did not place GPT-4.5 beyond the existing comparison models. METR cautions that its short evaluation of an earlier checkpoint may underestimate capabilities.

evidence_items.locator: Appendix, introductory paragraph and Model evaluation scores
evidence_items.explanation: Reported GPQA scores rose from 53.6% to 71.4%, and AIME scores from 9.3% to 36.7%, compared with GPT-4o. These substantial domain gains challenge an unqualified dismissal, but do not establish a major advance toward AGI.

evidence_items.locator: Opening paragraph; methodology distinguishes final training runs from research spending
evidence_items.explanation: The analysis separates company-wide expenditure from final training runs and research experiments. Its aggregate estimate cannot substantiate billions spent specifically developing GPT-4.5.

unresolved_gaps: No model-specific total development expenditure with a matching accounting basis was established.
Multiple years of GPT-4.5-specific development were not independently established.
The evidence does not translate uneven benchmark improvements into a settled measure of progress toward AGI.
A representative review sample was not established.
